topSignals.title: FERC large-load interconnection ruling due tomorrow (June 18)
topSignals.text: FERC has pinned its long-awaited decision on Docket RM26-4-000 — large-load grid interconnection reform for data centers and heavy industry — to June 18. The ruling follows a DOE-directed ANOPR from Oct 2025 and comes one day ahead of FirstEnergy's concurrent proposal (filed June 5) urging FERC to require data centers to fund their own transmission upgrades rather than socialising costs. Separately, FERC already approved PJM's Expedited Interconnection Track on June 9: up to 10 shovel-ready projects ≥250 MW per year can fast-track to online within 3 years; effective July 31, expires end-2027. The June 18 ruling is the single most consequential regulatory event for SOFC competitiveness this month — a lenient cost-allocation outcome would ease grid-connected alternatives; a strict "developers pay" outcome reinforces SOFC's behind-the-meter advantage. (FERC commitment; Utility Dive: PJM fast-track; Utility Dive: FirstEnergy filing)

topSignals.title: Nebius + Bloom Energy: $2.6B master fuel cell capacity agreement (May 14, 2026 — first coverage)
topSignals.text: European AI neocloud Nebius entered a Master Fuel Cell Capacity Agreement with Bloom Energy covering 328 MW initial capacity (three 10-year phases, $2.6B total contract value). First phase expected live in 2026. Bloom installs, operates, and maintains; Nebius purchases power output — effectively a SOFC-as-a-service PPA model. Deployment at Nebius AI data center sites. This is the first European AI-cloud operator to sign a large SOFC capacity agreement and establishes a repeatable commercial structure. (Nebius newsroom; Fierce Network; Yahoo Finance analysis)

topSignals.title: Crusoe pauses 1.8 GW Cheyenne AI factory (June 10) — uncovered risk to Bloom backlog
topSignals.text: Crusoe halted development of Project Jade (1.8 GW AI Factory in Cheyenne, WY) at a customer's request, causing Bloom Energy stock to drop >10% on June 10. Bloom was contracted to supply ~900 MW of SOFC for the first phase (alongside AEP); the project's pause clouds ~$2.65B of potential BE-linked revenue. Partial offsets: (a) Black Hills Corp (grid infrastructure provider) confirmed it is working directly with the end customer and still expects the project to proceed by early 2028; (b) the Nebius $2.6B deal partially replaces the backlog signal. Net effect: headline risk to Bloom's volume ramp, but not a cancellation. Monitor customer identity and 2028 restart timeline. (Motley Fool: Bloom plunge; TS2 Space: Crusoe pause; KuCoin: Crusoe halts WY)

items.text: Quiet day. No new stack, manufacturing, or efficiency announcements from Bloom, Ceres, Elcogen, Sunfire, SolydEra, or Mitsubishi since June 15 digest.

Nebius + Bloom $2.6B (328 MW) — see Top Signals #2. PPA-style delivery model (Bloom owns and operates; Nebius buys power) is emerging as the dominant commercial structure for large SOFC deployments. First phase live 2026.

Crusoe Cheyenne pause — see Top Signals #3. Black Hills expects 1.8 GW project to resume by early 2028; Bloom retains Oracle (2.45 GW), Brookfield ($5B), AEP ($2.65B), and Equinix (100 MW+) as confirmed pipeline items not affected.

FERC June 18 ruling (tomorrow): See Top Signals #1. Key watch: whether the Commission adopts strict cost-allocation for large loads (strengthens SOFC BTM case) or adopts a socialised transmission cost model (reduces BTM premium). (FERC; HData blog: what it means)

FERC approves PJM Expedited Interconnection Track (June 9): 10 shovel-ready projects ≥250 MW/year, online within 3 years, effective July 31, 2026; expires end-2027. Developers fund 100% of network upgrades + post $500K study deposit + $15K/MW readiness. Speeds grid-connected alternatives — slight competitive headwind for SOFC BTM in PJM region, but cost burden and 3-year lead time still much longer than SOFC's 90-day advantage. (Utility Dive; MGrId)

FirstEnergy FERC filing (June 5): Proposes data centers pay 100% of transmission upgrade costs needed for interconnection (analogous to gas pipeline precedent). If adopted by FERC June 18, raises cost of grid-connected alternatives; SOFC BTM deployment unaffected. (Utility Dive; Energy Central)
Quiet day. No new SMR, gas turbine, or battery announcements since June 15. FERC PJM fast-track (above) is the only structural shift; applies to generators, not directly to demand-side.
Fuel cell stocks — June 15 session: BE +7%, FCEL +1%, PLUG +2%. YTD: BE +219%, FCEL +135%, PLUG trailing. Bloom share price ~$278, market cap ~$79B. (24/7 Wall St. June 15)
Analyst targets raised: Daiwa and UBS revised BE price targets to $260–$320 range; Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight with $310 target. Consensus: 74% Buy. (StocksToTrade: BE rally)
Ceres Power (CWR:LON): +22% week-on-week following June 10 capital raise close; cumulative 1,000%+ gain over past year; market cap ~£1.2B ($1.6B). (Bitget News)

MS-SOFC comprehensive review (Springer, 2026): "Comprehensive review of current trends and future directions of metal-supported solid oxide fuel cell: From materials to applications," published in the International Journal of Minerals, Metallurgy and Materials. Provides systematic analysis of MS-SOFCs as next-generation energy conversion devices — covers materials selection, fabrication, and durability pathways relevant to INOCEL technology benchmarking. DOI: 10.1007/s12613-026-3402-0

Second MS-SOFC review (Springer, April 2026): "A comprehensive review on the progress and evaluation of metal supported solid oxide fuel cells (MS-SOFC)," Journal of Solid State Electrochemistry. Covers performance metrics and scale-up pathways. DOI: 10.1007/s10008-026-06571-7

lcoe.text: FERC PJM fast-track cost signal (NEW): Grid-connected alternatives in PJM now face $500K study deposit + $15K/MW readiness deposit + 100% network upgrade funding. For a 250 MW project: ~$3.75M upfront + network upgrades (often $10–50M/project). Raises effective cost of grid-connected power vs. SOFC BTM for US East Coast projects. (Utility Dive)
NG price: no new data this cycle. EIA Henry Hub baseline from June 10 digest ($3.34/MMBtu FY2026 avg) remains current. Monitor EIA Thursday weekly report.
